subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Poverty of the Stimulus
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Poverty of the Stimulus.

hook.text: A child says "I goed to the park." Nobody taught her that rule. She invented it from patterns.

buildup.text: Chomsky argued that speech children hear is too messy for them to learn grammar from it alone.

discovery.text: He proposed Universal Grammar: an inborn system that constrains what grammars children can learn.

twist.text: Critics countered: statistical learning can extract grammar. Babies detect syllable patterns at eight months.

climax.text: Current evidence suggests some innate bias combined with powerful statistical learning from input.

punchline.text: Grammar is partly born, partly heard.

quiz.question: What is Universal Grammar?
options: An innate system constraining possible grammars
